title: Penetration Testing
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Penetration Testing.

items: OWASP Testing Guide — Web application security testing
NIST SP 800-115 — Technical Guide to Information Security Testing
PTES — Penetration Testing Execution Standard
OSSTMM — Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual
Methodology ensures consistent, repeatable, and thorough testing
Black Box (Zero Knowledge) — Tester has NO prior knowledge of the target
White Box (Full Knowledge) — Tester has COMPLETE knowledge (source code, architecture)
Gray Box (Partial Knowledge) — Tester has SOME knowledge (user credentials, network maps)
Black box simulates external attacker; white box simulates insider threat
White box is most thorough; black box is most realistic

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: White box testing finds MORE vulnerabilities because testers can analyze source code and architecture. Black box testing is more REALISTIC but may miss deeply embedded flaws.

items: Written agreement defining scope, boundaries, and expectations
Specifies what systems can be tested and what techniques are allowed
Defines time windows for testing (avoid business-critical hours)
Includes emergency contacts and escalation procedures
Legal authorization must be obtained before any testing begins
Scope — Which systems, networks, applications are in scope
Excluded systems — Systems that must NOT be tested
Allowed techniques — Social engineering, physical, network, application
DoS testing — Usually prohibited or heavily restricted
Data handling — How sensitive data found during testing is handled
Communication — How findings are reported (especially critical ones)
Timeline — Start date, end date, testing windows
Legal protections — Indemnification and liability

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Penetration testing without proper written authorization is a CRIME (unauthorized access). Always get signed rules of engagement before testing.

items: Planning/Scoping — Define scope, objectives, rules of engagement
Reconnaissance — Gather information about the target (passive and active)
Scanning/Enumeration — Identify live systems, open ports, services
Exploitation — Attempt to exploit discovered vulnerabilities
Post-Exploitation — Determine what access was gained, pivot to other systems
Reporting — Document findings, evidence, and recommendations
Passive — No direct interaction with target (OSINT, DNS lookups, social media)
Active — Direct interaction with target (port scanning, service enumeration)
Executive summary (for management)
Technical findings with evidence
Risk ratings for each finding
Remediation recommendations
Retesting plan
